thread:
jamie: Opening with customer case C-3921 — customer reports chat stream stalls mid-response, then client reconnects and receives duplicate truncated chunk. Happening ~3-5x/day for a single org behind Cloudflare + ALB. Logs attached.

tom_customer: seeing half of the assistant reply then stream stops, client reconnects and gets the rest but with a gap/dup. Happens across browsers and our mobile app. No 5xx from API.

jamie: Repro steps customer provided:
1) curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \ 
   -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACT' \
   'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=xx'
2) wait ~75-95s, stream yields 1 partial event then connection closes.

anna: quick question — are they on Dedicated or Hosted? Any custom routing?

jamie: Hosted. Region: us-west-2. Through Cloudflare spectrum -> ALB -> internal Envoy.

oliver: Can you paste an excerpt from the proxy logs around a failure? Specifically Connection: close or FIN events. Also the request id for the root event.

jamie: log snippet (redacted request_id=rid-9a3):

```
[2026-03-15T12:21:04Z] rid-9a3 ACCEPTED client_ip=1.2.3.4 route=/v1/streams
[2026-03-15T12:22:46Z] rid-9a3 proxied_to=alb-01 status=200 keepalive=idle
[2026-03-15T12:23:18Z] rid-9a3 upstream=- conn=FIN reason=idle_timeout
[2026-03-15T12:23:18Z] rid-9a3 downstream=reset client_closed=true
```

maria: ALB idletimeout defaults to 60s unless we set it. But logs show upstream FIN at ~134s after start — suspicious. Cloudflare could be reusing different TCP connection and causing half-close. Also saw gzip filter firing.

oliver: That FIN at 12:23:18 is after 134s from accept (matches client-observed stall). If ALB idle timeout were 60s we'd expect earlier — maybe ALB TCP keepalive misalignment with Envoy's stream semantics. Envoy by default can half-close and buffer data. Do we have proxy_buffering on at nginx or envoy filter that could aggregate chunks until window flush?

anna: Config check: Envoy has "stream_idle_timeout" unset (inherits route timeout). Our ALB is configured to 350s for long-lived streams by default in other tenants; this customer came through a legacy path with 120s. Cloudflare edge idle is 90s. Mix of 90/120/350 could cause midstream half-close depending on which hop holds the TCP.

jamie: Repro attempt from support lane with curl while hitting edge directly (bypassing Cloudflare) — stream still truncates at ~95s occasionally. When we send server-side comment keepalive every 30s it stays open.

oliver: That suggests lack of application-level heartbeat is required for some proxies. For a mitigation, propose we:
- Insert SSE comment keepalive every 25s: ":\n\n" or ": keepalive\n\n" on streams for older clients.
- Disable gzip/chunk aggregator on the path for streaming endpoints.
- Ensure ALB idle timeout >= 300s for Hosted streaming pool and align Cloudflare origin keepalive.

maria: Also recommend setting Envoy config: "common_http_protocol_options: { idle_timeout: 0s }" for streaming route and enable "tcp_keepalive". For nginx fronting we should set "proxy_buffering off; proxy_set_header Connection ''; proxy_http_version 1.1;".

jamie: I documented mitigation steps to customer and asked for permission to toggle gzip and add keepalive comments. They asked for a timeline.

deploy-bot: Scheduled change window: 2026-03-17 02:00 UTC (infra patch) — will apply gzip off and adjust ALB timeout in canary hostpool.

tom_customer: Thanks. FYI when we added keepalives in our app it looked much better. Happy to test infra changes in canary.

oliver: Follow-ups for eng-runtime:
- Add default SSE keepalive at 25s for streaming endpoints (configurable per-tenant).
- Add a runtime flag to opt-out if customers manage keepalives themselves.
- Add observability: measure first-silence duration and count reconnections per request_id.

anna: I'll own the infra rollout for ALB + Cloudflare origin settings. Jamie will coordinate with customer for canary test. Moving to escalation tag: #escalate-eng-runtime and pinging eng-runtime on-call.

jamie: Pinging eng-runtime on-call: @oliver — can you review the runtime change? Also attaching the customer's packet capture (pcap) showing TCP FIN immediately followed by a new SYN from client.

oliver: Will triage tomorrow. Initial hypothesis: mixed idle timeouts + proxy buffering + missing app keepalives -> partial outputs + reconnect loop. Proposed long-term fix: runtime-level keepalive + better doc for customers about proxy config. Thanks.
